strengths: The content is well-organized and easy to follow.
The motivation is well-established and the effectiveness of their solution is verified by extensive experiment.
The proposed architecture achieved competitive performance on a wide range of tasks, while maintaining competitive efficiency.

Although the boundary and reflection cues have been explored in previous works, the paper shows that a better network design that focuses on low-level features may improve the segmentation of mirrors and glass surfaces/objects.
The paper provides extensive comparisons on eight benchmarks, which shows an overall picture of this topic.
The paper is generally easy to read and understand.
The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performances on multiple datasets.
The paper is overall well-written and nicely structured.
weaknesses: The authors regard the boundary loss as their contribution, but do not provide an ablation of this module.
Similarly, the reflection loss also has not been ablated.

The authors claim that their proposed approach is robust to generic semantic segmentation tasks, but do not evaluate on the most widely used semantic segmentation datasets, such as ADE20K and cityscapes.
The influence of different pretraining of the backbone is not properly assessed.

The authors claim that most semantic segmentation models struggle to distinguish between glass and non-glass regions, but does this assertion still hold true for the state of the art generic semantic segmentation model, such as SAM?

The paper creates a lot of models (TransCues -T, -S, -M, -L, -B1, -B2, -B3, -B4, -B5) with inconsistent backbone choices across tables, making the comparisons very messy and lacking meaningful analysis or discussion of selection criteria.
The Abstract mentions that the RFE module "decomposes reflections into foreground and background layers", but section 3.3 lacks the corresponding designs and motivations.
Section 3.4 uses pseudo ground truth reflection masks, but it is not mentioned how these pseudo labels are created.

The paper only discusses RFE with (Zhang et al., 2018) regarding reflection modeling and does not consider using reflection removal methods (e.g., ICCV’21 "Location-aware Single Image Reflection Removal") to generate pseudo labels.
The boundary loss seems not a novelty; the paper needs to explain the novelty or move it to the supplemental and discuss existing methods such as the IJCV’22 paper and PMD (Lin et al. 2020).
The feature flow in the RFE module (Figure 7 of supp.) is rather complicated and more explanation is helpful to evaluate its novelty.
The placements of RFE and BFE seem casual; more explanation of the design rationale is needed.
The ablation study only includes the RFE and BFE, while it is not known how much contributions the FEM, FPM and the final MLP have made to the segmentation performance.

The model relies on the detection of reflections, but it is unclear whether reflections can always be detected for glass surface/object segmentation and how this affects the final results; failure cases shown are dataset-specific and should include limitations of the proposed model.
In Fig. 5, does it show that the proposed method is consistently effective for different backbones? This should be better discussed.
In Table 6, it would be nice to show the computation complexity of the two designed modules for analysis.
How to theoretically verify that the proposed method did really make use of reflection cues? This could be better discussed.

It is hard to find any novel operations in the proposed reflection feature enhancement module as it simply combines existing mechanisms; clarification of technical novelty and theoretical contributions is needed.

There are extensive segmentation methods that introduce boundary-relevant loss designs or other designs; incorporating some existing boundary-relevant designs for a comparison would better show the superiority of the proposed boundary feature enhancement module.
The related work follows that of Trans4Trans; it would be nice to add more recent related state-of-the-art works.
